problems: These tools are left out of this turn; tell the user, and fix the configuration when you can:
config:
Configures this chat page, which has no settings panel: its endpoints, model, system prompt, tools, display, style and every other setting. It runs lines of the KiSS CLI, one command per line; all lines of one call apply together or not at all, so batch related changes in a single call. Changes apply at once to the running configuration, and a call answers with what changed: the old line after -, the new one after +. Only the user keeps them, by typing /save <name>; load <name> goes back to a save, reset back to the site defaults: tell them so once a change looks right.
Commands: set <module> <key> [name] <value> | no <module> <key> [name] | no <module> <name> | show <module> [key] [name] | show <module> <name> | show running | show models | show style | show saves | show diff <save> <save> | load <save> | reset. A save is a name; show diff reads session as the running configuration.
A key is two fixed words, a module then a key; a key of a collection such as endpoints takes the item name next; the value always comes last. A line that stops short lists what may follow it: set lists the modules, set display its keys. show models lists the models of every endpoint under ! <endpoint>; set chat model takes a line of it as is. An MCP server, set mcp url <name> <url> and its bearer set mcp key <name> <key>, gives you its tools; show tools lists every tool by who serves it, and set tools use <name> off hides one. show style lists the style of the page, its tokens under :root (show style | include :root); set css sheet <name> <css> restyles anything over it, the sheets applied by name, so one sheet holds one change. Words abbreviate (sh run). Filter any output with | include <pattern>. Quote values holding blanks.
Example call:
set css sheet accent ':root { --accent: oklch(0.62 0.21 300) }'
set endpoints url pod http://localhost:8080/v1
show css
